metadata.title: Migrating to Opus 4.5
metadata.subtitle: The Model Migration Skill
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: does migrating to Opus 4.5 also fix anything that behaves differently on the new model, or does it only touch the model string? Lands the carry-out that migration touches a string, a header, and one parameter — never the prompt — unless you ask.
metadata.anchor_pair: NB04 -> NB08 (the same model-call line, before migration and after)
metadata.one_flag: N/A - direct mechanism description throughout (see SCRIPT.md register audit)

beats.narration_text: Someone asked how to upgrade their code to Opus 4.5. Not upgrade — migrate: the string changes, but nothing about how Claude behaves gets touched unless you ask. So — how do you migrate to Opus 4.5?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'How do I upgrade my code to Opus 4.5?', hesitates on 'upgrade', corrects to 'migrate', lands the real question

props.text:
How do I
upgrade my code
to Opus 4.5?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('upgrade' -> 'migrate') lands on screen.

beats.narration_text: Say your code calls Claude on Sonnet 4.0, Sonnet 4.5, or Opus 4.1, and it's time to move it to Opus 4.5.

production_viz.label: TIME TO MOVE MODELS
production_viz.mechanic: Chip row: SONNET 4.0, SONNET 4.5, OPUS 4.1, arrows into OPUS 4.5 (accented).
production_viz.caption: three models, one destination

beats.narration_text: The natural guess: migrating swaps the model string and quietly smooths over anything that behaves differently on the new one.

shot.new_visual_element: The wrong guess: migration also fixes behavior

production_viz.label: THE NATURAL GUESS
production_viz.mechanic: Chip row: NEW MODEL STRING, arrow to SMOOTHED-OVER BEHAVIOR (accented) — sell the guess as reasonable.
production_viz.caption: migrate sounds like it means both

beats.narration_text: It doesn't. The skill touches exactly four things — a model string, a beta header, one parameter, and a summary — and not one word of your prompts.

shot.new_visual_element: The closed list that breaks the guess

production_viz.label: FOUR THINGS, NOTHING ELSE
production_viz.mechanic: Chip row, no arrows: MODEL STRING, BETA HEADER, EFFORT PARAM, A SUMMARY — a closed, concrete list.
production_viz.caption: zero prompt words, by design

beats.narration_text: Take the line that calls the model. Right now it names Sonnet 4.5, and it's carrying a header for a beta context window.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — the model-call line, before migration

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — one call, before
production_viz.mechanic: A monospace code card: model = "claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929" plus a beta-header line. THIS EXACT CARD FRAME RETURNS AT NB08.
production_viz.caption: one call, in your code today

beats.narration_text: The skill searches your whole codebase for calls like it first, then updates every one it finds — using the right string for whichever platform you're on: Anthropic's own API, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, or Azure AI Foundry.

production_viz.label: SEARCH, THEN UPDATE EVERY PLATFORM
production_viz.mechanic: Chip row: ANTHROPIC API, AWS BEDROCK, GOOGLE VERTEX, AZURE AI FOUNDRY.
production_viz.caption: same model, four different strings

beats.narration_text: Along the way it drops that beta header if the new model doesn't support it yet, and sets an effort parameter to high.

shot.new_visual_element: Two small edits that ride along

production_viz.label: TWO EDITS THAT RIDE ALONG
production_viz.mechanic: Chip row: REMOVE BETA HEADER, arrow to SET EFFORT: HIGH.
production_viz.caption: two small edits, every time

beats.narration_text: One model never moves in this pass: Haiku. Sonnet and Opus calls migrate; Haiku calls stay exactly as they are.

production_viz.label: ONE MODEL STAYS PUT
production_viz.mechanic: Chip row: SONNET → MIGRATES, OPUS → MIGRATES, HAIKU → UNTOUCHED (accented, the exception).
production_viz.caption: on purpose, not an oversight

beats.narration_text: Back to that same line: it now names Opus 4.5, the beta header is gone, and effort is set to high — one call, four small edits, nothing else touched.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — the same call, migrated

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — the same call, after
production_viz.mechanic: THE NB04 CARD FRAME RETURNS, identical layout: model = "claude-opus-4-5-20251101", beta header line replaced by a comment, effort = "high" added.
code_lines: # beta header removed — 1M context not yet supported
production_viz.caption: same call, migrated — nothing else touched

beats.narration_text: If your code only ever called Sonnet or Opus, that's the whole job: it searches, swaps, and tells you exactly what it changed.

production_viz.label: THE CLEAN CASE
production_viz.caption: clean case: done in one pass

beats.narration_text: But if Opus 4.5 actually behaves differently once it's running — say it starts firing tools too eagerly — the skill won't touch your prompt for that on its own. Report the specific behavior, and only then does it make a targeted adjustment.

production_viz.label: OPT-IN, NEVER BY DEFAULT
production_viz.mechanic: Chip row: BEHAVIOR CHANGES, arrow to YOU REPORT IT, arrow to THEN IT ADJUSTS (accented).
production_viz.caption: opt-in, never by default

beats.narration_text: Migrating to Opus 4.5 only touches the model string, a header, and one parameter — it never changes your prompts unless you ask it to.

props.quote: Migrating to Opus 4.5 only touches the model string, a header, and one parameter — it never changes your prompts unless you ask it to.
props.sparkLine: Migrate the string. Never the prompt.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Open Claude Code in a project that calls a Claude Sonnet or Opus model, and paste this: Search this codebase for Claude model strings and migrate them to Opus 4.5 — Anthropic API, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, or Azure AI Foundry, whichever you use. Remove any one-million-token-context beta header you find, add an effort parameter, and summarize every change. Watch two things: does it leave every Haiku string untouched, and does it change so much as one word of your prompts without asking first?

props.command: Search this codebase for Claude model strings and migrate them to Opus 4.5 — Anthropic API, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, or Azure AI Foundry, whichever you use. Remove any one-million-token-context beta header you find, add an effort parameter, and summarize every change.
